blocks.text: Authentication Service (formerly ZIdentity) supports user attributes and session attributes that are necessary to configure SAML-based single sign-on (SSO) access for users. For both these attributes, Authentication Service allows you to define custom attributes in addition to the default system-defined attributes.

By default, Authentication Service provides 14 system-defined user attributes for user identities and 6 session attributes for user sessions. Based on your organization's requirements, administrators can also define custom user and session attributes for more granular access control. For example, Authentication Service can retrieve user and session attributes and make them available to Private Access (ZPA) and relevant policies can be applied.
Attributes provide the following benefits and enable you to:

blocks.item: Use the user attributes in Zscaler services (e.g., Internet & SaaS (ZIA), Private Access) for policies.
Use the attributes for Just-in-Time Provisioning (JIT) and System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM) provisioning through an external identity provider (IdP).
Use the session attributes in Internet & SaaS Identity Proxy and Private Access service policies.

blocks.text: The following table lists the system-defined attributes in each category:

table: displayname firstname lastname nickname primaryemail department organization title division costcenter usertype formattedname manager addresses
created_at last_authenticated_at identity_provider is_device_managed is_device_compliant is_device_domain_joined

blocks.text: On the Attributes page (Administration > Authentication > Attributes), you can do the following:

blocks.item: Import a CSV file that contains a list of user attributes.
Delete multiple user attributes. This option is visible only when you select more than one user attribute.
View a list of system-defined and user-defined user and session attributes. By default, the User Attribute tab is selected. For each user attribute, you can see:
Display Name: The name that is visible throughout Authentication Service.
Attribute Name: The name of the attribute with proper syntax.
Data Type: The data type (String, Integer, Boolean, etc.) of the attribute.
Required: Whether the user attribute is a mandatory requirement.
Origin: Whether the attribute is system-defined or user-defined. You cannot edit or delete a system-defined attribute.
Select attributes to perform bulk deletion. Select more than one user attribute to view the Delete option.
Click the Session Attribute tab to view session attribute details and add a session attribute.
Session attribute can only be used when the user is authenticated by an IdP.
Select the required session attribute in the IdP configuration to make sure that they are passed to Zscaler services (e.g., Internet & SaaS, Private Access) during authentication.
